name: Act of June 8, 1858 confirming the sale of the Christian (Munsee) Indians' four sections in Kansas
aka: An Act to confirm the Sale of the Reservation held by the Christian Indians
nations: Munsee or Christian Indians (Royce), the Moravian Munsee then living among the Delawares in Kansas
promises: Not a treaty. The Act recites that Article 13 of the Delaware treaty of May 6, 1854 granted four sections of land to the Christian Indians, patented to them on May 21, 1857.
It confirmed their sale of the four sections to A. J. Isacks for $43,400, a sum the Act called fair consideration, once Isacks paid it to the Secretary of the Interior for the Indians.

The proceeds were to buy a permanent home, buildings, stock and tools for the Christian Indians, with the balance invested for a school; land bought for them could be divided in severalty and was not to be sold without the President's approval.
today: Royce records that a new home was found for the Christian Indians among the Swan Creek and Black River Chippewa in Kansas, with whom they confederated (Royce p. 821; treaty of July 16, 1859). No court, claims-commission or government finding of a breach was found.

sources.title: Act of June 8, 1858, ch. 122, 11 Stat. 312 (An Act to confirm the Sale of the Reservation held by the Christian Indians)
Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule pp. 820-821

openQuestions: treaties.json names this entry for the Delaware and gives the Delaware Nation, Oklahoma as present-day tribe. Royce's tribe column reads 'Munsee or Christian Indians', and the Act concerns the Christian Indians' four sections. Not edited.
Royce lists no area number of its own for this entry ("See 317"); the four sections lay inside the Delaware cession of 1854.

The present-day successors of the Kansas Christian Munsee were not settled here; Royce (p. 841) says Delaware, Chippewa, Munsee and Shawnee later moved from Kansas and merged with the Cherokee Nation.
Whether Isacks paid the $43,400 and how the fund was used was not traced.

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for: Court of Claims names "munsee", "christian indians", "delaware" (none on the 1858 sale); ICC full text "Isacks", "Munsee Kansas 1858" (0), "Christian Indians", "Christian Munsee". The Delaware Docket 27-A opinion of 1959 (https://cdm17279.contentdm.oclc.org/digital/collection/p17279coll10/id/386) mentions a "Christian Indian tract of 2,571 acres" near Fort Leavenworth only as a comparison sale when valuing the Delaware Outlet; it makes no finding about this sale. Nothing new.
